description: A feature flag in the load generator's `locustfile.py` activated a `flood_home` Locust task (weighted 5/32, ~16% of selection per cycle) that fired `flood_count = 100` rapid GETs to the frontend homepage; outbound HTTP request rate from the load generator spiked, driving container CPU and network traffic on the frontend and frontend-proxy containers above baseline.
mechanism:
The flag is read in [`locustfile.py#L220`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/load-generator/locustfile.py#L220), inside the load generator's Locust test suite.

Each simulated user repeats this loop:

1. Execute one randomly-chosen task (weighted)
2. Wait for `wait_time` (1–10 seconds, [line 114](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/load-generator/locustfile.py#L114))
3. Go back to step 1

One iteration of that loop is a "cycle." Each user runs independently and concurrently. There are **5 simulated users** (see [`.env#L101`](../../opentelemetry-demo/.env#L101)).

`flood_home` has a **5/32 (~16%) chance** of being selected each cycle. When selected, it sends `flood_count` rapid requests to the homepage. The `flood_count` value is **100**, defined in [`demo.flagd.json#L105`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/flagd/demo.flagd.json#L105).

variants.description: Load-generator container total CPU usage rate spiked ~2.3x to drive the flood traffic
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline averages roughly 1.1e7–1.4e7 nanoseconds/sec with occasional spikes to ~2e7. At 15:28, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to 4.96e7 — approximately 4x the baseline — and remains elevated (frequently 2.5e7–5.1e7) for the rest of the window. This is the first sustained departure above baseline after the incident time.

variants.description: Network bytes received by load-generator container surged ~28x from HTTP response data flowing back from the flood of homepage requests
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates roughly 364-888 bytes/s. At 15:28, one minute after the incident, the value jumps to ~39365, which is ~45x the baseline average (~540). This is the first clear spike above normal levels.

variants.description: Network bytes received by frontend-proxy container surged ~21x as the load generator's flood_home task sent 100 rapid HTTP GET requests per invocation through the Envoy proxy
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates roughly 570-1513 bytes/s. At 15:28, one minute after the incident time, the value jumps to ~45389, which is ~30-50x the baseline average. This is the first clear spike above normal levels.

variants.description: Frontend container total CPU usage rate spiked ~5x to serve the flood of homepage requests
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates roughly between 9e6 and 2e7. At 15:28, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to 1.47e8 — approximately 10x the baseline — representing a clear, sustained spike in frontend container CPU usage.

variants.description: Total bulk index attempts in Jaeger's OpenSearch backend. Tracks the same span volume increase as inserts (~5.5x).
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is roughly 6-7. At 15:28, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to ~13.0, nearly doubling the baseline. This is the first clear departure from the baseline range.

logs.name: load-generator: User flooding homepage 100 times (INFO)
logs.description: Starting at 15:27:16.798 UTC and continuing through 15:36:18.729 UTC, load-generator emitted 25 flood_home logs confirming loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is ON with value 100. The downstream effect is visible in frontend-proxy Envoy access logs as a surge in homepage GETs starting at 15:27 UTC (baseline ~1-3 req/min through 15:26, climbing to 100-502 req/min during 15:27-15:36), all returning HTTP 200.
logs.cause: Direct effect of the loadGeneratorFloodHomepage feature flag. When flagd returns a value > 0, locust's flood_home task starts a user_flood_home span (attribute flood.count=100) and logs 'User flooding homepage {flood_count} times' before issuing that many GET / requests against frontend-proxy.
